title: Fog
whatItIs: Fog cuts how far you can see, sometimes suddenly. Slow down so you can stop within the distance you can see.

keyFacts.text: You MUST use headlights when visibility is seriously reduced, usually when you can't see more than 100 metres.
You MUST NOT use fog lights unless visibility is seriously reduced, and MUST switch them off when it improves.

keyFacts: Drive slowly enough to stop well within the distance you can see is clear.
Don't follow the tail lights in front: they give a false sense of safety.
At junctions with a poor view, stop and listen for traffic, then go when you are sure it is safe.

items.title: Lights
items.text: Dipped headlights. Fog lights only when you can't see more than about 100 m.

items.title: Speed
items.text: Slow enough to stop within the distance you can see.

items.title: Distance
items.text: Leave a big gap. Don't hang on to the tail lights ahead.

items.title: Junctions
items.text: Stop, listen for traffic, then go when you are sure it is safe.

b.label: Fog lights off
points: They dazzle and hide brake lights

onTheTest.question: When must you switch off your rear fog lights?
options: When you enter a 30 mph area
Only at the end of your journey
onTheTest.why: Fog lights must be switched off as soon as visibility improves, because they dazzle drivers behind and can hide your brake lights.

traps: Fog can be patchy: a clear stretch can suddenly turn thick again.
The tail lights ahead don't show you a safe gap.
Fog lights left on after the fog clears dazzle drivers and hide your brake lights.
